facts.text: District Heights Apartments, later Woodland Springs, opened in phases from 1949 to 1951 as a 925‑unit Colonial Revival complex for veterans and federal workers.
In 1946, the remaining 300 acres of undeveloped land were purchased by New York City builder Samuel R., sparking the town’s growth.
By 1926, District Heights had about 25 homes, two businesses, a grocery store, a filling station, a pump house, and a free Model T bus.
The 1940s saw Cape Cod–style houses spring up in District Heights, built with Federal Housing Administration financing for returning veterans.
The first streets of District Heights, Halleck and Aztec, were laid out by 1925, marking the town’s earliest organized layout.
The District Heights library opened in 1987, honoring the area's 19th‑century Spaldings election district that later became Spauldings.
